statement: The PM2.5 concentration field is spatially uniform across Multnomah County at each hour
rationale: Only two regulatory monitors sit inside the county, so any spatial interpolant would fit two points and manufacture gradients the data cannot support
affects: Absolute exposure per agent and whether placement differences arise from exposure gradients or only from travel time
sensitivity_plan: Compare against inverse-distance weighting over all 7 tri-county monitors, adopted only if it beats the uniform field in leave-one-out cross-validation

statement: All residents evacuate simultaneously at the first crossing of the PM2.5 threshold on or after a shelter opens
rationale: PARTIALLY MITIGATED. The original defect - evacuation on the brief Sept-7 spike, days before the real shelters opened - is fixed: with respectShelterOpeningDates=1 residents cannot depart until an operating shelter is actually open (OCC 2020-09-10, CJ 2020-09-11), so departure now occurs 2020-09-10 07:00, the first threshold crossing after opening. What REMAINS assumed is simultaneity: every resident departs on the same tick because no awareness or decision-delay model is implemented. Real departures would be staggered by awareness, which the one sourced behavioural parameter (0.35 awareness, PSU Stories from the Outside) could inform
affects: Absolute exposure magnitudes and arrival timing; currently an acknowledged artefact
sensitivity_plan: Compare the gated runs against the archived ungated production runs (documented in FINAL_RESULTS_REPORT); implement the PADM staged-departure model and sweep the departure-delay distribution

statement: 2025-26 campsite report locations represent the September 2020 spatial distribution of unsheltered residents
rationale: No 2020 records exist in the open feed; the locations are real City of Portland reports but temporally displaced by five years
affects: Network distance to shelter for every agent and therefore all travel and exposure results
sensitivity_plan: Compare against alternative spatial hypotheses such as population-weighted or uniform placement to bound sensitivity to origin geography

statement: Each operating shelter has a nightly capacity of 99
rationale: Newsroom-sourced and consistent across contemporaneous reports but not confirmed by a primary agency document. Unchanged by the vulnerability layer, and now the single largest driver of the headline result: the number sheltered equals total capacity exactly in every run
affects: Whether capacity binds and therefore all refusal and equity outcomes
sensitivity_plan: Confirm against a primary source and sweep capacity while refusal counts are being quoted

statement: Every mapped street centerline is walkable by pedestrians
rationale: Freeway and ramp segments are not yet filtered from the pedestrian graph although the classification attributes needed to do so are present in the data
affects: Shortest-path distances and therefore travel time and exposure for agents whose route would otherwise use a freeway
sensitivity_plan: Filter by street classification and compare routed distances before and after

statement: Pedestrians are not bound by one-way vehicle restrictions so the street graph is undirected
rationale: Pedestrian movement is not constrained by vehicle direction of travel and treating the walking graph as undirected is standard
affects: Shortest-path distances
sensitivity_plan: none - structural

statement: A resident admitted to a shelter remains there for the rest of the event
rationale: No departure behaviour is modelled within the nine-day event window because arrival is the study endpoint
affects: Peak and final occupancy are identical and capacity never frees up
sensitivity_plan: Model departures only if a research question requires them; currently out of scope

statement: Shelter admission is first-come first-served rather than needs-based triage
rationale: No documentation of a triage policy at the September 2020 clean-air shelters was found
affects: Which agents are admitted once capacity binds and equity outcomes at production population scale
sensitivity_plan: Compare against a vulnerability-prioritised admission policy as an explicit scenario

statement: Susceptibility weights are 1.0 so the Exposure Burden Index equals raw exposure
rationale: The slide-cited relative risks could not be verified and the multiplicative formulation is a category error, so the weights remain inert
affects: The Exposure Burden Index and its Gini coefficient carry no susceptibility signal
sensitivity_plan: Report exposure stratified by susceptibility group as the primary metric and sweep weights 1.0-2.5 only as a labelled equivalent-dose sensitivity

statement: The declared shelter arrival radius is not applied
rationale: The parameter is declared and recorded in the manifest but consumed by no code path because agents terminate exactly at shelter-adjacent street nodes
affects: Nothing at present - but a reader of the manifest may wrongly believe a 200 m arrival radius is in force
sensitivity_plan: Either consume the parameter in the arrival test or remove it from the manifest and the parameters file

statement: The modelled population consists of adults only
rationale: Six unsheltered minors were counted (0.3%), every mobility and susceptibility parameter adopted is an adult parameter, and unaccompanied-minor services differ structurally
affects: Population composition and the denominator of every rate reported
sensitivity_plan: none - structural; recorded as a scope limitation

statement: All residents know the shelters exist and where they are
rationale: A placeholder pending the awareness stage, contradicted by the local record in which 65% of surveyed unhoused residents never heard about the shelters
affects: Uptake rate and therefore every outcome that depends on who attempts to shelter
sensitivity_plan: Replace with an awareness Bernoulli of 0.35 and sweep 0.25-0.45

statement: Every resident walks at the same constant speed (heterogeneity disabled only)
rationale: RESOLVED for the final study runs. With enableHeterogeneity=1 each resident samples its own comfortable gait speed from the Bohannon & Williams Andrews 2011 age-by-sex means with CV 0.13 from Bohannon 1997, and mobility-limited residents take the Boyce ambulant-impaired distribution by replacement. The single constant survives only in heterogeneity=0 runs, which exist to reproduce the archived baseline byte-identically
affects: Travel time and time outdoors for every agent and therefore who arrives and who fails to
sensitivity_plan: Sweep the coefficient of variation 0.10-0.17 and the mobility-aid mix; compare heterogeneity=0 against =1 at equal seed

statement: Endpoint claims of one street-node identifier within 100 m are the same physical junction
rationale: Legitimate endpoint scatter in the source data is sub-metre while the smallest corrupt displacement observed is about 1.65 km, so the threshold separates two well-separated regimes
affects: Street-graph topology and therefore every routed distance
sensitivity_plan: Vary the tolerance across the empty band between the two regimes and confirm the corrected graph is unchanged

statement: Cumulative exposure is an index rather than an inhaled dose
rationale: No breathing rate or particle deposition is modelled, so the quantity is a time-integrated concentration and not a mass inhaled
affects: The units and interpretation of the headline exposure metric
sensitivity_plan: Replace with an inhaled mass via the specified and evidence-backed ventilation chain

statement: A resident refused at a full shelter re-routes from its current position
rationale: TRUE AS IMPLEMENTED since the Finding-A fix: on refusal the resident remains at the refusing shelter's street node and plans its next leg from that node; no return-to-encampment movement exists in the model. Guarded by the failing walked-vs-planned-route check in scripts/analyze_run.py (walked <= planned_route_m + snap_gap_m + 200 m; agents.csv QC columns planned_route_m, snap_gap_m, door_refusals) and exercised by an archived capacity-binding reference run. The remaining assumption is behavioural: instant re-decision at the door with no queueing or abandonment
affects: Travel distance and accrued exposure for every refused resident; at production scale this is the entire cohort that selected a shelter which later filled
sensitivity_plan: Behavioural alternatives (queue at the door, abandon evacuation, return to encampment as a modelled choice) are future work; until then the walked-vs-planned failing check runs on every analysed run

statement: Agent execution order within a tick does not affect outcomes
rationale: True only while shelter capacity never binds; at the demonstration population of 50 agents against 198 beds agents never interact
affects: Which agent receives the last available bed once capacity binds at production population scale
sensitivity_plan: Introduce order-independent two-phase admission before any run with more agents than beds, then confirm results are invariant to seed-driven ordering

statement: Mobility limitation is sampled with an age gradient borrowed from a California donor population
rationale: The local PIT gives only the marginal (19.2%, itself a lower bound) with no age breakdown. Sampling mobility independently of age is known to be wrong - it under-represents compound-vulnerability residents, the exact group the study exists to find - so CASPEH's 22%-overall vs 32%-at-50+ RATIO is applied while holding the measured local marginal exactly. The gradient is donor-imputed; the total is measured
affects: Which residents walk slowly, and therefore the measured access disparity between mobility-limited and unimpaired residents
sensitivity_plan: Sweep independent vs conditional sampling and the 0.19-0.27 prevalence range; report whether the access disparity survives independent sampling

statement: Every mobility-limited resident walks as an unaided ambulant impaired person
rationale: No source gives the aid-type mix (cane/crutches/walker/wheelchair) for this population, and 03-MOVEMENT.md directs that the mix be swept rather than asserted. The category chosen is the FASTEST of Boyce's impaired categories, so the modelled mobility penalty is deliberately conservative. CASPEH's finding that 20% of a 22% mobility-limited population use an aid suggests aid use is in fact common, so real speeds are likely LOWER and the measured access disparity likely LARGER than reported
affects: Walking speed of mobility-limited residents, and therefore their travel time, exposure and shelter access rate
sensitivity_plan: Sweep the aid mix across Boyce's categories (0.57-0.95 m/s means) and report the access disparity as a range

statement: Shelters open at 00:00 local on their recorded opening date
rationale: The shelter source records dates, not hours. Midnight is the earliest defensible reading and therefore the one most generous to the shelter system; real sites opened later in the day, so pre-opening outdoor exposure is UNDERSTATED. The direction of the bias is known and stated rather than tuned
affects: Departure time and therefore the absolute pre-departure exposure accrued by every resident
sensitivity_plan: Re-run with opening at 12:00 and 18:00 local to bound the effect on absolute dose; relative outcomes are unaffected because all residents share the same trigger

statement: A resident refused for capacity waits at that shelter and re-attempts when another shelter opens
rationale: Extends decision D-6 to a world where shelters open on different days. Treating REFUSED_ALL_FULL as terminal left Charles Jordan's 99 real beds entirely unused, which is a modelling artefact rather than a finding. The resident therefore waits where it stands - never returning to its encampment, which remains unmodelled - and sets out again when a second site opens. What is assumed is perfect knowledge of that opening and willingness to wait outdoors for it
affects: Whether the second shelter fills at all, and the travel-time distribution, which now includes waiting for an opening
sensitivity_plan: Model awareness-limited knowledge of openings and an abandonment probability once a resident has been refused

statement: Inhalation rate is identical for every resident regardless of asthma or COPD status
rationale: Audited and deliberately retained. No defensible population-specific ventilation multiplier for adults with asthma or COPD during walking was identified; obstructive disease alters breathing PATTERN in ways that do not translate cleanly into inhaled volume per minute, so any figure would be an assumption wearing a citation. Consequence: the exported exposure is a time-integrated concentration index, not an inhaled mass. Standard wording: asthma and COPD increase susceptibility to smoke exposure but were not converted into extra inhaled dose because no population-specific dose multiplier was identified
affects: Whether vulnerability can act through dose as well as through time outdoors; currently only the latter is modelled
sensitivity_plan: If a sourced ventilation multiplier is obtained it drops into the existing vwe_ugm3h column, which is built for it and inert at 1.0

statement: Asthma has no effect on walking speed
rationale: Researched rather than assumed by default. The literature supports lower total, moderate and vigorous PHYSICAL ACTIVITY among adults with asthma, but no verified quantitative comfortable-gait-speed decrement was found. Borrowing the COPD estimate (V24) for asthma would be an invention. The asymmetry between the two conditions in the results is therefore a consequence of evidence availability, not of a modelling preference
affects: Whether residents with asthma show an access disparity; currently they do not, while residents with COPD do
sensitivity_plan: Adopt a speed decrement only if a comfortable-gait-speed estimate for adults with asthma is published; otherwise report the asymmetry explicitly

statement: Scenario C total shelter capacity equals the simulated population and is a demonstration only
rationale: DEMONSTRATION SCENARIO, NOT REAL AVAILABILITY. Total capacity is set to 2037 so that beds stop being the binding constraint and the exposure effect of travel alone becomes visible. The total is bounded rather than arbitrary: it sits inside the 1900-2200 person range that Multnomah County's ENTIRE current year-round shelter system provides once published bed/room/unit/family counts are converted (SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT section 3). Relative site capacities stay 1:1, matching the equal capacities the 2020 source reports, so shelters still fill in sequence and residents still redirect
affects: Every Scenario C result; must never be presented as September 2020 shelter provision
sensitivity_plan: Report Scenario C only alongside Scenario A and always with its label; sweep intermediate capacities to trace the dose-response between 198 and 2037 beds

statement: Ventilation rate depends only on whether a resident is walking
rationale: Two activity states are modelled - walking and outdoors-but-stationary - using EPA Exposure Factors Handbook activity-level rates. No age, sex, body-mass, load or health effect on ventilation is applied, because none was sourced for this population. Deliberately excludes any diagnosis-based term: that would smuggle biology into a physics quantity
affects: Inhaled dose for every resident, and therefore the magnitude of the placement effect measured in dose
sensitivity_plan: Sweep walking 1.2-2.0 and resting 0.4-0.8 m3/h; add the EFH age gradient if the primary table is obtained

statement: The placement experiment holds total system capacity equal to the population
rationale: DESIGN CHOICE, not a claim about 2020 availability. Both arms give the two-site system 2037 spaces so that total capacity cannot bind and shelter PLACEMENT is the only difference between arms. Individual sites keep finite capacity, so shelters fill, residents are refused at a full door and re-route. An earlier design capped both arms at 198 beds, which made capacity rather than geography determine the outcome and left the experiment with no power to detect a placement effect
affects: Every A/B result. The historical 2x99 capacity is retained only as a separate reference run for calibration against observed occupancy
sensitivity_plan: Sweep intermediate system capacities between 198 and 2037 to trace where capacity starts to dominate placement

statement: The heavy-belongings prevalence is the midpoint of a sourced bracket rather than a measured local value
rationale: The bracket is real (floor 10.8% Ozarks 2024 unsheltered PIT N=138; ceiling 42-46% CASPEH 2023 / Herring et al. 2020 N=351) but no Multnomah estimate exists, so the 0.284 midpoint is a declared assumption inside verified bounds. The mechanism (decision latency and abandonment, never a speed penalty) is anchored to the JOHS spokesperson's contemporaneous account (Street Roots 2020-09-16)
affects: Departure timing and destination choice for residents with heavy belongings; the size of the barrier-attributable access gap
sensitivity_plan: Sweep the full bracket 0.108-0.46 and report whether the barrier-attributable access gap survives at the floor

statement: Phase-E decision attributes are sampled independently of each other and of the health attributes
rationale: No correlation data exists for this population: no source jointly measures awareness, belongings, pets and dependents among unsheltered adults. Independence is declared rather than silently adopted; realized joint prevalences are exported in every manifest so the sampled population is auditable
affects: Joint prevalence of compound-barrier residents - the group most likely to be missed by interventions
sensitivity_plan: Report realized joint prevalences in the manifest; if a correlation source emerges resample with a copula and compare the compound-barrier access gap

statement: Pet intake policy is RECORDED for the present-day network and unrecorded only for the 2020 shelters and the theoretical new sites
rationale: CORRECTED 2026-07-29 after an adversarial review found the original statement false for the arms actually being run. The record is SILENT for the September 2020 clean-air shelters (six county releases plus Street Roots checked; contrast the co-located Red Cross evacuation shelter which explicitly welcomed pets). It is EXPLICIT for the present-day 2026 network: shelters_multnomah_2026.csv carries pets_allowed for all 48 facilities and 4 of them record admit (Laurelwood Center, River District Navigation Center, Walnut Park Shelter, Willamette Center = 422 beds). The derived per-arm files had dropped that column, so the model was asserting refusal at 422 beds whose own source records admission and pet owners came out at exactly 0 percent sheltered. Fixed by scripts/build_shelter_policy_elayer.py, which joins the recorded policy into _elayer variants selected by shelterPolicyVariant=1; the archived per-arm files are left untouched so data_version_tag is unchanged. petPolicyDefault still governs only the genuinely unrecorded sites: 3 facilities absent from the inventory plus arm C's 10 theoretical new sites. Refusal remains the conservative default there because 48.1 percent of owners report ever being turned away over pet policy (Henwood et al. 2020)
affects: Eligibility of the ~11.7 percent of residents with pets and therefore their access and exposure; before the correction this was a categorical exclusion rather than a partial one
sensitivity_plan: Sweep petPolicyDefault across both worlds {admit refuse} for the unrecorded remainder and report pet-owner outcomes under each; report the recorded-policy share of beds per arm alongside

statement: The departure-hazard intercept alphaHazard is provisional pending the E9 historical calibration
rationale: No direct estimate of baseline departure odds exists. The initial value is chosen so the implied attempt share matches the sourced attempt pipeline (0.356 aware x 0.385 attempt-given-aware = 13.7%); the E9 calibration against the observed ~130/198 occupancy and ~90/40 site split will replace it with a fitted value and an ablation showing which mechanism carries the fit
affects: Absolute departure rates and every absolute count downstream; relative arm comparisons are less sensitive because all arms share the intercept
sensitivity_plan: Fit to the E9 target then sweep +/-1 log-odds around the fitted value; report fit failure plainly if the target cannot be reproduced

statement: The outreach-contact conversion rate lambdaOutreachPerDay is unsourced
rationale: No outreach-contact rate for unhoused residents during the September 2020 event exists in the record; the parameter is anchored only loosely to the survey finding that 75% received no information during the wildfires. It is the sole awareness-conversion channel while L3 word-of-mouth stays deferred
affects: How many initially-unaware residents ever learn shelters exist and how late; the awareness-attributable share of non-arrival
sensitivity_plan: Sweep 0-0.2 per day including 0 (no outreach) and report awareness conversion counts per arm

statement: Believed admission likelihood scales with shelter size (fillRisk-as-size-prior)
rationale: No queue-avoidance or rejection-belief estimates exist for shelter-seeking during smoke events. The betaS x ln(capacity) term is a declared stand-in: residents are assumed to believe larger sites are likelier to admit them. Impedance dominance and a positive supply term are verified in the destination-choice literature (Cheng Wilmot & Baker 2008) but the specific functional form is a modelling choice
affects: Destination choice under L1 and therefore which sites fill first and who is refused at the door
sensitivity_plan: Sweep betaS/betaT over 1-2 orders of magnitude around the published supply/distance marginal rate of substitution; compare against betaS=0 (pure nearest)

statement: The Scenario-E synthetic smoke series are constructed counterfactuals; v2 is anchored to the worst verified urban wildfire-smoke hour on record
rationale: Both series are built by scripts/build_smoke_severe.py as labeled transforms of the hash-verified observed Sept-2020 Multnomah AQS series: every hour scaled by a constant and the main episode stretched by whole days, with the two-spell structure preserved exactly as observed. TWO-TIER ANCHOR, verified 2026-07-30 against agency and peer-reviewed primaries: (1) v2's 4.436x makes the synthetic peak equal the worst VERIFIED hourly PM2.5 over an intact non-evacuated city - 2496.1 ug/m3, Florey station, Canberra, night of 5-6 Jan 2020, computed directly from the ACT Government's raw open-data records (dataset 94a5-zqnn; official CHO report cites the same 2496; the widely quoted ~5000 Canberra number is an AQI index, and Monash's true hourly max was 1926.0); worst official urban 24-h mean from the same event: 1147 ug/m3, Monash, 1 Jan 2020 (ACT SoE 2023). (2) The documented all-source ceiling is 5229 ug/m3 hourly at a Fort McMurray community site in May 2016 (Landis et al. 2018, doi 10.1016/j.scitotenv.2017.10.008, SHARP regulatory monitors; network-wide industrial max 6106) - cited as ceiling, deliberately NOT scaled to, because those monitors sat in/adjacent to the burn perimeter of an evacuated town, breaking the sheltering-population-in-an-intact-city premise. v1's 1.75x (peak 984.75) is retained as the intermediate severity arm; the earlier Palisades comparison remains corrected (LA regulatory hourly max 301.1 was below Portland's own 562.7). Importing any real foreign series was considered and deferred: the model's county-uniform mean would dilute a spatially localised plume
affects: Every Scenario-E exposure and dose number; these must never be reported as observed magnitudes
sensitivity_plan: Sweep effective severity via smokeScale (V47) around each embedded transform; report all Scenario-E results only as counterfactual, naming the anchor (Canberra 2496.1) and the ceiling (Fort McMurray 5229) explicitly

statement: The Scenario-E street closures are constructed schedules; the worst-case family's timing and class structure are evidence-anchored while its weights are declared
rationale: No documented pedestrian street or bridge closure INSIDE the Portland metro core during the September 2020 smoke episode was found, so no schedule can be reconstructed; all schedules are seeded draws with a connectivity check guaranteeing no shelter is isolated (a closure set can never manufacture unreachability at a shelter door). The EVIDENCE BASE, verified 2026-07-30 across events: (TIMING) major-road closures began within hours of onset in every severe event examined - Camp Fire lost key egress arteries ~2-3 h after its 06:20 ignition with 23 documented burnovers (NIST TN 2252, doi 10.6028/NIST.TN.2252); the Delta Fire closed ~45 mi of I-5 the same afternoon it started (Sept 5 2018); Lahaina's Honoapiilani Hwy closed from 6:20 a.m. on day one (Aug 8 2023, downed poles, with fire closures by afternoon); Almeda closed I-5 same-day (Sept 8 2020); PCH closed on day one of the Palisades fire - and closures ACCUMULATED over days (the ODOT statewide list grew Sept 8-11 2020, all before Portland's smoke peak). Smoke alone, with no flame at the road, closed I-75 (~00:15 Jan 29 2012, Paynes Prairie visibility event, 11 deaths in the pileups after premature reopening). Documented durations span hours (I-75 ~3.25 h) to days (Delta ~5 d) to weeks (Eagle Creek I-84: 10-19 d) to months (PCH ~4 mo; OR-224 ~19.5 mo) - the model's permanent-once-closed rule is the registered worst-case tail of that distribution. (CLASS STRUCTURE) the named closure record is arterial/highway dominated in every event and those closures are deliberate formal orders (ORS 810.030, OAR 734-020-0150: each road authority closes its own highways), while local streets demonstrably closed via debris/downed lines (Grants Pass 6th and G St, Sept 2020 - verified) but are under-enumerated because DOT feeds report DOT roads; arterial dominance in the record is therefore partly REPORTING ARTIFACT. WHAT REMAINS ASSUMED: the numeric class weights (local-street weight justified only by mechanism + reporting-bias argument; bridge weight PURE assumption - no documented wildfire river-bridge closure was found anywhere), the wave sizes, and the mapping of documented same-day highway closures onto pedestrian-relevant city streets
affects: Route lengths and travel time and therefore exposure for every resident walking during or departing after a closure wave; the size of any C-over-A redundancy advantage; who faces the V51 decision at all
sensitivity_plan: Sweep closuresCode {0 base extreme worst} and closureDraw across seeded draws; report closure effects as a range across draws, never from a single schedule; sensitivity-test the assumed local-street and bridge weights

statement: Push-through and stuck mechanics at a blockage are declared modelling decisions with indoor-fire and vehicular anchors only
rationale: No study estimates what pedestrians do at a smoke-obstructed urban street closure or what it costs them. Three quantities are therefore declared rather than cited: the probability of being delayed (V49, no analog found anywhere), the length of that delay (V50, hour scale bracketed only by vehicular incident and hurricane-evacuation delays), and the trait threshold that selects pushing over rerouting (V51, whose coefficients are unsourced but whose population-level outcome is checked against the fire-incident turn-back band: 26-30% of smoke-movers turned back in Wood 1972 / Bryan 1977, 45% in Jin 1997's dense-smoke corridor). The decision rule deliberately REUSES the already-registered risk trait theta_i (V35) and barrier cost c_i (V40) instead of introducing a second risk construct; the mobility/encumbrance coupling has no quantitative anchor and its direction is labeled plausible-but-undemonstrated. Every anchor is indoor/tunnel fire smoke or vehicular traffic - none involves outdoor wildfire smoke at physical street closures - so TRANSFERABILITY IS ITSELF ASSUMED. Being stuck is a delay rather than a terminal state so no unfalsifiable harm outcome is created
affects: Who reroutes and who gambles at a blockage; the dose difference between those two populations
sensitivity_plan: Sweep all three parameters over their registered ranges and report whether the reroute-vs-push split by burden survives at the conservative end; report the realised push-through share against the 55-75% continue band (V51); report the no-closure arm alongside so the mechanism's contribution is separable
